summary: Built an IKEv2/IPsec site-to-site tunnel between node1 and node2 (OPNsense 26.1) over their shared transit network (172.16.100.0/30), carrying private traffic between node3's lan-a (10.50.10.0/24) and node4's lan-b (10.50.20.0/24). Configured via swanctl (strongSwan/vici) model in config.xml: new opt1 (transit, static) and opt2 (private LAN, static) interfaces on each firewall, a PSK-authenticated IKEv2 connection with a tunnel-mode child SA covering the two private CIDRs, and firewall rules permitting IKE/NAT-T/ESP on the transit interface plus a pass rule on a manually-registered 'ipsec' (enc0) pseudo-interface for decrypted traffic (required because OPNsense's core filter compiler only recognizes interfaces present in config.xml's <interfaces> section, not the plugin's dynamic-only ipsec interface list). node3/node4 got static private IPs and routes to the peer subnet via ens7, persisted through /etc/network/interfaces.d. Verified end-to-end: ping between 10.50.10.2 and 10.50.20.2 succeeds, and tcpdump on the transit link during a ping showed only ESP packets (no plaintext), confirming encryption in transit. All four nodes were then restarted one at a time (preserving the other three throughout), each showing a changed boot identity (kern.boottime for the OPNsense nodes, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for the Ubuntu nodes) and full recovery: OPNsense nodes auto-restored their opt1/opt2 interfaces, pf ruleset, and IPsec SA (strongswan auto-started and re-established); Ubuntu nodes' static ens7 config and routes persisted via ifupdown, and end-to-end ping across the tunnel succeeded after each of the four restarts.
actions_performed: Mapped cluster topology by testing point-to-point connectivity across vtnet1/vtnet2 on node1/node2 and ens7 on node3/node4 to identify transit vs lan-a vs lan-b links

Configured static transit IPs (172.16.100.1/.2) and private LAN gateway IPs (10.50.10.1, 10.50.20.1) as new opt1/opt2 OPNsense interfaces on node1 and node2 via config.xml edits + configctl interface reconfigure
Generated a PSK on node1 via openssl and passed it to both nodes' config scripts using secret_env (never placed literally in command text or final report)

Created a swanctl IKEv2 site-to-site connection (PSK auth) plus local/remote/child entries in config.xml on node1 and node2, enabled IPsec (root <ipsec><enable/>), and reloaded (configctl ipsec reload)
Added firewall pass rules for IKE (udp/500), NAT-T (udp/4500), and ESP on the transit (opt1) interface, and a pass rule on private LAN (opt2)

Diagnosed and fixed a filter-compile issue where a rule targeting the 'ipsec'/'enc0' pseudo-interface was silently disabled by registering a real config.xml <interfaces><ipsec> entry (if=enc0) so OPNsense's Firewall\Plugin interface mapping recognizes it
Assigned static private IPs (10.50.10.2, 10.50.20.2) and peer routes on node3/node4, persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-ens7.cfg
Verified encrypted end-to-end connectivity: ping 10.50.10.2<->10.50.20.2 succeeds, and tcpdump on the transit interface during the ping shows only ESP packets
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot identity + IPsec/interface health) on all four nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially (one at a time), polled each until exec was available again, confirmed changed boot identity (kern.boottime / boot_id), and verified full recovery of interfaces, pf, IPsec SA, and end-to-end tunnel connectivity after each restart
